moat_against: Commodity price-taker: crush/merchandising margins are market- and policy-set, no pricing power
Thin structural margins; filed net income fell 2023 ($2.243B) to 2025 ($816M)
Working-capital-heavy: conservative OE negative in 3 of last 5 years; TTM OE -$6.32/share
Viterra capex step-up ($1.749B TTM) and share issuance (195.7M diluted) unproven through a down-cycle
moat_for: Combined Bunge+Viterra origination/storage/port/crush footprint in 50+ countries, hard to replicate
Largest global oilseed-processing position; specialty oils and renewable-feedstock optionality
Integration traction: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $9.25-9.75, $2B Viterra buyback completed
Century-old merchant with balance-sheet staying power through cycles
moat_justification: Post-Viterra origination, storage, port and oilseed-processing network at hard-to-replicate global scale with demonstrated flow-rerouting optionality and integration traction (FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised, $2B deal buyback completed), against commodity price-taker economics on both sides (crush/merchandising margins market- and policy-set), ~1%-of-revenue structural margins, falling filed net income 2023-2025, a working-capital model that made conservative OE negative in 3 of the last 5 years, and unproven-through-a-cycle Viterra capex/integration paid for partly in dilutive shares.
name: Bunge Global SA
one_liner: Global agribusiness scale post-Viterra but commodity price-taker economics and negative TTM cash OE, moat 5/10 — at $107.01 the median-base DCF yields a 5.3% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $24.15 (Tier F on the TTM base); it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$24.
